formCues: Stand tall, avoid leaning on handles
Push and pull arms in rhythm with legs
setup: Step onto the arc trainer pedals, grip the moving or stationary handles, and select a resistance level before starting the stride.
commonMistakes: Leaning body weight onto the handles
Taking short, shuffling strides
Slouching forward at the hips

formCues: Set kickstand foot lightly on ball of foot
Keep chin tucked and ribs down
setup: Upper back braced on a bench, load across the hips, one foot flat and the other staggered back on its toes in a kickstand position.
commonMistakes: Overloading the kickstand leg
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout
Letting knees cave inward

formCues: Keep ribs down and core tight
setup: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet hip-width, holding the handles or ends in front of the thighs.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to generate lift
Raising arms above shoulder height
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears

setup: Anchor a band at elbow height to your side, elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked against the ribs, forearm starting rotated outward.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the body
Using shoulder or torso rotation instead of the forearm
Moving too fast to feel the rotator cuff work

setup: Anchor a band overhead, kneel or sit facing the anchor, and grip the band with arms extended overhead.
commonMistakes: Using body lean instead of lat contraction to pull
Shrugging shoulders during the pull
Only partially extending arms at the top

setup: Stand on the band with feet hip-width apart, holding handles at the sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
commonMistakes: Shrugging traps to lift the arms higher
Swinging the torso for momentum
Raising hands above shoulder height

formCues: Keep elbows pointed forward and stationary
Keep core braced to prevent arching
setup: Anchor the band underfoot or low behind you, hold the other end overhead with elbows bent and pointed forward.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drift outward or backward
Arching the lower back for extra range
Not fully extending the arms at the top

setup: Stand perpendicular to a band anchored at chest height, holding the band with both hands at the sternum, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Letting the torso rotate toward the anchor
Pressing with arms only instead of bracing the trunk
Standing too close, reducing band tension

setup: Stand tall holding a light band with both hands, arms extended straight out in front at shoulder height.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to cheat the range
Using momentum instead of controlled pulling
Shrugging shoulders up during the pull

formCues: Keep body in a straight line
Drive through palms to press up
Keep band secured across upper back
setup: Loop a band across the upper back and under both hands in a push-up position, hands slightly wider than shoulders.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag or pike up
Band slipping off the hands mid-set
Flaring elbows out to 90 degrees

formCues: Keep chest up and core braced
Push knees out in line with toes
setup: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width, band looped over the shoulders or held at the chest, anchored under both feet.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Rising onto the toes when standing up

formCues: Load into a quarter squat before jumping
setup: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width, band anchored under the feet and looped over the shoulders or held at the chest.
commonMistakes: Landing stiff-legged instead of absorbing impact
Losing band tension mid-jump
Letting knees collapse inward on landing

formCues: Lead with elbows out to the sides
Squeeze shoulder blades at the top
setup: Stand on the band with a slight forward hip hinge, holding handles crossed in front of the body with arms extended.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright and using arms instead of rear delts
Using momentum to swing the arms back
Rounding the lower back

formCues: Keep chest up and shoulders back
setup: Anchor the band at chest height in front of you, holding the handles with arms extended and feet staggered or together for stability.
commonMistakes: Using body lean instead of back muscles
Shrugging shoulders during the pull
Not fully extending arms at the start

formCues: Use a wide grip for less mobile shoulders
Move slowly through the full arc
setup: Stand holding a light band or PVC pipe with a wide overhand grip in front of the thighs, arms fully extended.
commonMistakes: Gripping too narrow and forcing the range
Bending the elbows to complete the arc
Rushing the movement instead of moving slowly

setup: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding handles at shoulder height with elbows bent.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to press up
Pressing the band forward instead of straight up
Shrugging shoulders at lockout

setup: Stand on the band with feet hip-width apart, holding handles at the sides with arms fully extended.
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders instead of a straight up-down path
Using momentum from the knees
Bending the elbows to assist

formCues: Rise onto the balls of the feet
setup: Stand on a band looped under the balls of both feet, holding the ends at shoulder height for resistance.
commonMistakes: Bouncing at the bottom instead of controlling the stretch
Not reaching full extension at the top
Bending the knees to cheat the range

setup: Anchor a band at ankle height behind you, loop the other end around one ankle, and stand facing away from the anchor.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips rotate during the curl
Using momentum to swing the leg
Not controlling the eccentric return

setup: Anchor a band overhead, stand facing the anchor with a slight forward lean, and hold the band with arms extended overhead.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to turn it into a pushdown
Using body weight instead of lat contraction
Standing too upright, losing hip hinge

formCues: Flex the foot up toward the shin
Keep the leg still, isolate the ankle
setup: Anchor a band low, loop the other end around the top of one foot, and sit or stand with the leg extended in front.
commonMistakes: Moving the whole leg instead of just the ankle
Using momentum instead of a controlled flex
Not achieving full dorsiflexion range

formCues: Lead with elbows, higher than hands
Keep band close to the body
setup: Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding handles in front of the thighs with an overhand grip.
commonMistakes: Pulling too high and stressing the shoulder
Using a very narrow grip that increases impingement risk
Swinging the torso for momentum

formCues: Rotate through the torso and hips together
setup: Anchor a band low to one side, stand sideways to the anchor with feet shoulder-width, and hold the band with both hands near the hip.
commonMistakes: Moving only the arms without hip and torso rotation
Rounding the back during the pull
Using excessive momentum instead of controlled rotation

formCues: Use the band to reduce difficulty as needed
Catch yourself with hands if you lose control
setup: Kneel with ankles anchored, a band around the torso attached to a sturdy anchor in front to assist the lowering phase.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips flex, turning it into a fold instead of a lean
Dropping too fast without control
Insufficient band assistance leading to a hard fall

formCues: Rotate hip to open top knee
Keep hips stacked, don't roll back
setup: Lie on one side with knees bent about 90 degrees and a band around the thighs, feet stacked together.
commonMistakes: Rolling the hips backward to cheat range
Using momentum instead of controlled hip rotation
Letting the feet separate

formCues: Keep back flat and chest up
setup: Stand on a band with feet hip-width, gripping the ends or handles just outside the legs in a hip-hinge starting position.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back
Squatting the weight up instead of hinging
Letting the band slacken at the top

formCues: Drive knees out against the band
Keep lower back flat on floor
setup: Lie on your back with a band around the thighs, soles of the feet together and knees dropped open to the sides.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back excessively at the top
Using a small range of motion
Letting knees collapse inward on the way down

formCues: Push knees out against the band
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and a band positioned just above the knees.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward against the band tension
Pushing through toes instead of heels
Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the top

formCues: Extend hip, not just the knee
setup: Get on all fours with a band looped around one foot and anchored under the opposite hand or foot, torso stable.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to gain range
Kicking with momentum instead of a controlled hip extension
Rotating the hips instead of keeping them square

setup: Stand on the band with the other end looped over the shoulders and traps, feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine as you hinge
Bending the knees too much, turning it into a squat
Not hinging far enough to load the hamstrings

setup: Upper back on a bench, band positioned above the knees, feet flat on the floor shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward
Hyperextending the low back at the top
Pushing through the toes instead of heels

formCues: Hinge at the hips, not the knees
Squeeze glutes to finish standing tall
setup: Anchor a band low behind you, straddle it facing away, and hold the band between the legs with a slight hip hinge.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back during the hinge
Squatting instead of hinging
Not fully extending the hips at the finish

formCues: Keep torso stable on the bench
Extend hips, don't hyperextend the low back
setup: Lie face down on a bench with hips at the edge, a band looped around both ankles anchored behind you, legs hanging down.
commonMistakes: Using lower back extension instead of hip extension
Swinging the legs with momentum
Raising the legs too high, overarching the spine

formCues: Lift leg out to the side, not forward
setup: Stand with a band around both ankles or anchored to one side, holding onto support for balance.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso to swing the leg higher
Rotating the hip to substitute for true abduction
Using momentum instead of a controlled lift

formCues: Pull working leg across midline with control
setup: Stand sideways to an anchor point with a band around the ankle of the leg farther from the anchor, holding support for balance.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to assist the movement
Using momentum instead of controlled adduction
Leaning away from the working leg

formCues: Transition by driving elbows forward and up
Keep the bar close to the body
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with a false grip, arms fully extended and body relaxed before initiating the pull.
commonMistakes: Excessive kipping instead of controlled transition
Letting the bar drift away from the body
Failing to fully lock out at the top

formCues: Perform bottom-half reps, then top-half, then full reps
setup: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand shoulder-width grip, arms fully extended, ready to perform seven bottom-half, seven top-half, then seven full curls.
commonMistakes: Using body momentum to swing the weight
Letting elbows drift forward or backward
Rushing the partial reps and losing range precision

formCues: Push knees out in line with toes
Keep chest up and back flat
setup: Bar racked across the upper traps, feet shoulder-width apart, unrack and step back before initiating the squat.
commonMistakes: Knees caving inward on the ascent
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Rising onto the toes when standing up

formCues: Only go as deep as shoulder mobility allows
Press bar in a controlled vertical path
setup: Bar racked behind the neck across the upper traps, feet shoulder-width, grip slightly wider than shoulders.
commonMistakes: Forcing range beyond available shoulder mobility
Leaning the head too far forward to clear the bar
Arching the lower back excessively to press

formCues: Lower bar to mid-chest with control
Drive feet into the floor for stability
setup: Lie on a flat bench with eyes under the bar, feet flat on the floor, grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Flaring elbows to a full 90 degrees
Losing shoulder blade retraction mid-set
